First, note that the range of $\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡x$ is given by

$$
{0}^{∘}\le \theta \le {180}^{∘}.
$$

Note that the angle $\theta $ spans the first and second quadrants.

Since $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ is positive, our answer is an angle that lies in the first quadrant, where cosine is positive.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14035417/assets/ca39c4cde40b99fd40a11746a31398d82814268b2df706e3101ee88648c9e2d4.png)

From the values in the first quadrant, we see that

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
arccos\,(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})={45}^{∘}.
$$
